_what: Hand-written labels for titles an ARM produced on an `open` question
where the shipped ladder fell through to the question verbatim. These
are the only filings a candidate could get wrong that the baseline got
right, so they are the whole false-positive surface.
`good` = the title names the subject of the filing and is a defensible
permanent Concept ID. `bad` = it names nothing, or names the wrong
thing, and the question-verbatim safety net was the better outcome.
Keyed `shape::title` -- never on the run index or the answer text, so a
regenerated corpus reuses every label whose produced title is unchanged.
_judgment_calls: `open::Decidimos que el ledger de merges vive fuera del frontmatter` is
the contested one, and it is recorded as contested rather than quietly
AGAINST it: #646 ruled that an open question has no extractable subject
and must fall through. `Decidimos` is first-person and situational, so
a later session asking `¿donde vive el ledger?` about the same decision
files a differently-named object -- the very duplicate-detection defect
FOR it, and why it is labelled `good`: #646's rule is about extracting
a subject from the QUESTION. The clause rung reads the ANSWER, which
does carry a subject here, so the ruling does not transfer. The title
is declarative, specific, and names the decision; the alternative it
that somebody asked something about storage. And the shipped
declarative rung already files situational first-person titles on open
questions today (`Bruno quedó como responsable de la migración`), so
